title: Developer Fidelity Alignment: Integrator Kit & Onboarding Playbook
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
SUMMARY
This playbook describes the "Integrator Kit" approach to align developer expectations for response fidelity across Local Developer Runtimes, Hosted Redwood API, and Dedicated/Private deployments. It combines a lightweight SDK, telemetry contract, sample fidelity test-suite, migration checklist, and commercial guidance so partner integrations ship with predictable quality and predictable cost. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction, avoid repeat regressions caused by quantization/sequence-length interactions, and surface cost/latency trade-offs early in customer engagements.

AUDIENCE
- Platform and product engineers integrating with Redwood APIs or embedding Redwood SDKs in developer tooling.
- Solutions engineers and customer success teams onboarding customers migrating from local dev or self-hosted inference to Redwood hosted/dedicated modes.
- Developer advocates and partner engineers building Marketplace connectors.

GOALS
- Provide a small, reproducible fidelity test-suite engineers can run locally and in CI to measure parity across runtimes (local sim -> hosted -> dedicated).
- Define a telemetry contract (minimum signals) for debugging fidelity regressions and cost attribution.
- Document a step-by-step migration checklist with clear ownership, gating criteria, and rollback signals.
- Offer packaging & pricing guidance for integrators choosing default fidelity presets.

SCOPE AND NON-SCOPE
- In-scope: text generation/chat fidelity alignment, short-form embeddings, and reranking flows. Includes SDK samples for JS/Python, CI integration patterns, and observability dashboards.
- Out-of-scope: full model training workflows, custom model adapters for third-party LLM vendors (see third-party-model-adapters-design).

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
1) Quick start (integrator kit contents)
2) Fidelity test-suite and metrics
3) Telemetry contract (required signals)
4) Migration checklist (canary -> rollout -> rollback)
5) Packaging & pricing guidance
6) Design notes and engineering requirements
7) Roadmap and release notes
8) Appendix: API examples and CI snippets

1) QUICK START: WHAT'S IN THE INTEGRATOR KIT
- SDK bundle: lightweight NPM/PyPI packages (redwood-integrator-js, redwood-integrator-py) that wrap the Redwood API and provide fidelity-preserving defaults (max_tokens caps, deterministic sampling presets, KV cache warmup helpers).
- Fidelity test-suite: 150 curated prompts covering conversational, multi-turn, and long-context edge cases plus expected-checksum responses for deterministic configurations.
- CI integration recipe: GitHub Actions + CircleCI templates to run suite against multiple endpoints.
- Telemetry schema: example events, recommended tags, and a sample Grafana dashboard JSON.
- Migration checklist: owner roles, canary size guide, SLO regressions to watch, and cost-guard rails.

2) FIDELITY TEST-SUITE AND METRICS
Short description: The suite is intentionally small and deterministic so it can run quickly in CI while being sensitive to common regressions (tokenization differences, sampling temperature, quantization-induced word-choice drift).
Key metrics (computed per run):
- pass_rate (percentage of prompts matching expected-checksum under deterministic settings)
- token_delta_median (median difference in token count produced vs reference)
- semantic_similarity_median (embedding cosine median when run with canonical embed model)
- latency_p95 (milliseconds)
- cost_per_prompt_usd (estimated token pricing model)

Example expected outputs: the suite includes a JSONL file (checked-in to integrator-kit repo) where each row contains prompt_id, prompt_text, canonical_response_checksum, canonical_embedding_vector_id. CI uses the checksum and similarity thresholds to triage failures.

3) TELEMETRY CONTRACT (MINIMUM SIGNALS)
All Redwood integrations running in production must emit the following minimum signals to the customer's telemetry and to Redwood's observability pipeline (customer-permissioned):
- request_id (string)
- model_id (string)
- model_variant (string)
- runtime_mode (local|hosted|dedicated|private)
- sequence_length_in, sequence_length_out (integers)
- latency_ms (integer)
- tokens_input, tokens_output (integers)
- sampling_seed (if provided), temperature, top_p (floats)
- batch_size (integer)
- quantization_profile (string)
- fidelity_flag (string) - e.g., fidelity:high|medium|low
- test_suite_prompt_id (optional) - when running regression suite
- checksum_match (bool) - when applicable
These fields are sufficient for us to triage: (1) fidelity regressions, (2) cost spikes, and (3) sizing/latency anomalies.

Suggested tagging: tenant_id, route_id, environment (dev|staging|prod), sdk_version.

4) MIGRATION CHECKLIST (OWNER + STEP-BY-STEP)
Owners: Solutions Engineering (lead), Product Engineering (runtime), Customer Success (communication).
Pre-Canary
1. Confirm customer use-cases and target SLOs (latency p95 <= X ms, semantic_similarity_median >= 0.88, error_rate <= 0.5%).
2. Run fidelity test-suite against customer's local runtime and record baseline metrics.
3. Configure integrator SDK with "preserve-determinism" mode and run suite against Redwood hosted sandbox.
4. Validate telemetry contract is enabled and flowing to sandbox dashboards.

Canary (10% traffic or 50k monthly tokens, whichever is smaller)
1. Create canary route with identical config to production route except model_variant pinned to canary.
2. Monitor pass_rate, semantic_similarity_median, latency_p95, and cost_per_prompt every 30 minutes for first 24 hours.
3. Set automated abort triggers: pass_rate drop >= 5 percentage points, semantic_similarity_median delta >= 0.05, latency_p95 increase >= 30%. If triggered, abort and rollback to previous variant.

Rollout
1. If canary is healthy for 72 hours, schedule linear rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 12-hour observation windows.
2. After each step, run full fidelity test-suite in production traffic shadow mode (run requests in shadow and evaluate checksums without affecting response path).
3. Finalize rollback window for 72 hours post-100% rollout.

Rollback signals
- sustained semantic_similarity_median drop > 0.03 for 24h, or
- increased user-facing error rate > 1% for 30 minutes, or
- unexpected cost uplift > 20% for 1 hour.

5) PACKAGING & PRICING GUIDANCE
Default packaging suggestions when recommending fidelity presets to customers:
- "Balanced" preset: medium caching, mixed quantization (8-bit for matmul-heavy layers), sampling temp 0.7. Good for low-latency chat; recommended for self-serve.
- "High-fidelity" preset: reduced quantization, conservative pruning, pre-warmed KV cache, deterministic sampling for key routes. Recommended for enterprise workflows with strict semantic parity needs.
- "Economy" preset: aggressive quantization, higher batch sizes, fallback to lower-cost variant for non-critical routes. Recommended for high-throughput vectorization workloads.

Commercial notes: provide a fidelity addon SKU (monthly) that bundles: 1) additional fidelity test runs per month, 2) extended observability retention (90 days), 3) access to model-variant compatibility support. Pricing examples should tie to committed tokens and observability retention tiers. Include credit-based pilot pricing for initial integration (e.g., 200k tokens free + 30-day fidelity triage support).

6) DESIGN NOTES AND ENGINEERING REQUIREMENTS
High-level requirements (must be met by product engineering to support Integrator Kit):
- Runtime: provide an API parameter "preserve_determinism" that enforces fixed seeds, disables non-deterministic kernels, and returns canonical tokenization metadata.
- Telemetry: expose an ingestion endpoint for integrator-sdk telemetry with per-tenant sampling controls.
- Sandbox: maintain a sandbox model_variant pinned to a known config for integration tests.
- Canary tooling: automated route duplication and linear rollout orchestration (existing rollout API extension).
- Cost calculator: API-based estimator endpoint that accepts expected token histogram and returns per-prompt cost across model variants.

Minimal security/ops constraints:
- All telemetry carrying test_suite_prompt_id or checksum_match must be flagged as test data and not included in persistent eval datasets unless explicit consent is provided.
- Keys used in integrator SDK must support scoped TTLs and route-limited scopes to limit blast radius during canaries.

Requirements table (configurable knobs):
| Setting | Purpose | Recommended default | Owner |
|---------|---------|---------------------|-------|
| preserve_determinism | Ensure repeatable outputs for regression checks | true (for test runs) | runtime team |
| fidelity_preset | High/Medium/Low fidelity cost tradeoffs | Medium | product |
| max_tokens_per_prompt | Safety and cost guard | 1024 | solutions eng |
| kv_cache_warmup | Pre-warm cache to reduce first-token latency | enabled | runtime |
| telemetry_sample_rate | Controls volume of telemetry | 100% for canary, 1% for production | eng-sre |

7) ROADMAP & RELEASE NOTES
Roadmap (near term):
- Q4 2026: publish integrator-kit SDKs and fidelity test-suite; create hosted sandbox variant and provide pilot credits.
- Q1 2027: rollout preserve_determinism API parameter and basic canary automation in Console.
- Q2 2027: fidelity-addon SKU launch with observability retention tiers and automated fidelity advisor in Console.

Release notes (v1.0 — 2026-10-12):
- Deliverables: integrator-kit repo, fidelity-test-suite (150 prompts), sample Grafana dashboard, GH Actions recipe, pricing pilot guidelines.
- Known limitations: deterministic checks currently only supported on select model families; embedding-based similarity uses reference embed model ID and must be gated per-customer.

8) APPENDIX: API EXAMPLES AND CI SNIPPETS
A. Example API snippet (Python) — deterministic test run\
```python
from redwood_integrator import RedwoodIntegrator
client = RedwoodIntegrator(api_key="REDACTED", preserve_determinism=True)
resp = client.generate(route_id="acme-chat", prompt="Summarize the customer's account notes.", max_tokens=256, model_variant="sandbox-fid-v1")
print(resp.text)
# expected_checksum: 7a3b2c...
```
B. GitHub Actions matrix example (run tests against local and hosted):
```yaml
name: fidelity-ci
on: [push]
jobs:
  run-suite:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        runtime: [local, hosted]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run fidelity suite
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          ./tools/run_fidelity_suite.sh --runtime ${{ matrix.runtime }} --report results/${{ matrix.runtime }}.json
```

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q: What if a customer's local runtime inherently differs (different tokenizer)?
A: We require the Integrator Kit to include a tokenizer compatibility check. If mismatch is unavoidable, document the delta in the integration notes and prefer embedding-based similarity thresholds over checksum checks for content-sensitive routes.

Q: Can we run full fidelity checks on production traffic?
A: Never mutate production responses. Use shadowing to run checks in parallel and report checksum_match without impacting live responses.
